WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
Chapter 4 compared an activity-based budget with last year plus a percentage. Book 2, Chapter 3 split costs into fixed and variable parts. Both ideas are used again here.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: the head-office budget for 2028
Six packages ask for $1,260,000. The board funds the essential packages in full, reduces two and rejects the sponsorships. Figure F305-03 gives an approved budget of $1,100,000, $148,000 less than last year plus 4%.

EXAM TRAP   Requested is not approved
A zero-based budget uses the approved amount of each package. An answer that adds the requested amounts, or starts from last year's total, has not used zero-based budgeting.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: raising the juice price
Sales proposes a 5% price rise to $21.00 and expects to lose 3% of volume. Figure F305-11 compares the contribution margin: $7,380,000 now and $8,031,600 after the change.

EXAM TRAP   Include the lost volume
Multiplying the old volume by the new margin ignores the cases lost after the price rise and overstates the gain. Use the new volume with the new margin.
